jira.title: Jira
jira.subtitle: Point this at your Jira, run a query, and see exactly what comes back and where each issue would land here. It only reads: nothing is written to Jira, and nothing is saved in this app.
jira.settingsHint: Read from Jira and check what it returns, before anything is ever synced.
jira.readOnlyJira: Nothing goes to Jira: no new issues, no edits, no comments, no transitions.
jira.readOnlyApp: Nothing is saved here either: no organizations, no capabilities, no items.
jira.readOnlyBody: There is no import button on this screen and no hidden one. This is a reading, so you can decide whether the tracker and Jira agree before they are ever connected.
jira.connBody: The credentials live in the Supabase function and never in this page. You set them yourself in the Supabase dashboard; nobody here can read them.
jira.connSecrets: Three secrets are read by the jira-read function: JIRA_BASE_URL, JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN. When one is missing, the sentence above names it.
jira.projectsBody: What this token can see, so you can read your project keys without leaving the screen.
jira.projectsEmpty: This token can see no projects on that site.
jira.mapBody: Which of your Jira fields carries the organization, which carries the capability, and which carries the status. Nobody can guess this for you, which is exactly why this screen exists.
jira.mapShape: One Jira issue per organization and capability — the shape this app expects.
jira.mapIncomplete: Pick the organization field and the capability field. Until both are chosen, every issue is reported as missing them — which is true, and is about this screen rather than about your data.
jira.fieldsEmpty: No fields have been read from that site yet.
jira.foldArabicBody: Off, names must match exactly once invisible marks and spacing are ignored. On, tashkeel is dropped and أ إ آ read as ا, ى as ي, and ة as ه — the differences a hurried keyboard makes. Run it both ways and compare: folding can also collapse two genuinely different organizations, and where only one of them is here that would be a confident wrong match.
jira.statusBody: Which of your Jira statuses means planned, in testing, or live here. These are the statuses your own results carry — not every status on the site — so run the query first, then map them and the readings update without reading Jira again. A status left unmapped is reported on every issue that carries it, never guessed at.
jira.statusesEmpty: Run the query below first. The statuses to map are the ones your own issues turn out to carry.
jira.statusConflict: Two of your status words are the same word once spacing and case are ignored — ⁨{value}⁩ — and they are mapped to different things here. The first one wins, which is a coin toss; rename one in Jira or map them the same way.
jira.jqlBody: Your JQL is sent exactly as typed. It is not rewritten on the way out, and it is not stored.
jira.jqlExample: project = NPH AND updated >= -30d ORDER BY updated DESC
jira.jqlHint: One page at a time, up to 100 issues, and you can read the next page from the results below.
jira.noSchedule: This runs when you press the button and at no other time. There is no scheduled sync in this version, and nothing here runs in the background.
jira.tableLabel: The issues Jira returned, and where each one lands

summaryMatched.one: 1 resolves to an organization and a capability;
summaryMatched.other: {count} resolve to an organization and a capability;

jira.morePages: Jira has more issues for this query than have been read.
jira.allRead: Every issue this query matches has been read — Jira left no page after this one.
jira.effectsNone: Nothing resolved, so a sync would have nothing to write.
jira.effectsCreate: Would be recorded for the first time
jira.effectsUpdate: Would change what this app records
jira.effectsHeld: Edited here — a sync would leave it alone
jira.effectCreate: Would be recorded here for the first time
jira.effectUpdate: Would change what this app records — it says ⁨{from}⁩ today
jira.effectUnchanged: This app already records the same thing
jira.effectHeld: This cell was edited here, so a sync would leave it as ⁨{from}⁩
jira.linksLoading: Reading what this app already records…
jira.linksFailed: What this app already records could not be read, so what a sync would do cannot be shown. The readings above are unaffected.
jira.linksTruncated: This app records more links than could be read in one go, so a few issues may be shown as new when they are not.
jira.noApply: There is no apply button, and none is hidden. This version reads and reports; writing the rows back is a separate decision to be made after this has been run against real data.
jira.noEntries: Items are never created from Jira. There is nowhere on an item to record which issue it came from, so one written here could not be recognised or taken back on the next run.
jira.noNodes: Organizations are never created from Jira either. An unknown name is something for you to add deliberately, not a licence for Jira to invent hospitals in your map.
jira.orgArchived: That organization is archived here. It still matches, and it is still where this issue lands.
jira.useCaseRetired: That capability is retired here. It still matches, and it is still recorded against.
jira.presenceAbsent: The field ⁨{value}⁩ was not in the payload at all — either the field id is wrong, or the account behind the token cannot see it.
jira.presenceBlank: The field ⁨{value}⁩ is there and empty on this issue — somebody has to fill it in.
jira.valuesWere: It carried more than one value: ⁨{values}⁩. One issue names one organization and one capability, so this one is reported rather than chosen between.
jira.candidates: ⁨{value}⁩ answers to more than one of them: ⁨{names}⁩. Nothing is guessed here — rename one, or point the issue at the one you mean.
jira.duplicateClaimedBy: ⁨{key}⁩ claimed that pair first, and keeps it.
jira.reasonMatched: Resolves to an organization and a capability
jira.reasonIssueNoKey: Jira sent an issue with no key, so there is nothing to record it against
jira.reasonIssueNoFields: Jira sent this issue with no fields at all, which is what a query that asked for none returns
jira.reasonOrganizationMissing: No organization is named on this issue
jira.reasonOrganizationMultivalued: This issue names more than one organization
jira.reasonOrganizationUnknown: No organization here answers to that name
jira.reasonOrganizationAmbiguous: More than one organization here answers to that name
jira.reasonUseCaseMissing: No capability is named on this issue
jira.reasonUseCaseMultivalued: This issue names more than one capability
jira.reasonUseCaseUnknown: No capability here answers to that name
jira.reasonUseCaseAmbiguous: More than one capability here answers to that name
jira.reasonStatusMissing: No status is named on this issue
jira.reasonStatusMultivalued: This issue carries more than one status
jira.reasonStatusUnmapped: This Jira status is not mapped to any of the three used here
jira.reasonDuplicatePair: Another issue already claims this organization and capability
jira.catalogueFailed: This workspace's organizations and capabilities could not be read, so nothing can be matched against them.
jira.catalogueTruncated: This workspace has more organizations or capabilities than could be read in one go, so a name that is really here may be reported as unknown.
jira.errNetwork: The function could not be reached, so nothing was refused — the request never arrived. Check the connection and try again.
jira.errNoBaseUrl: JIRA_BASE_URL is not set on the jira-read function, so it does not know which site to call. Add it in the Supabase dashboard.
jira.errNoEmail: JIRA_EMAIL is not set on the jira-read function. Jira Cloud authenticates the account's email address together with its API token.
jira.errNoToken: JIRA_API_TOKEN is not set on the jira-read function. Create the token in your Atlassian account and add it in the Supabase dashboard.
jira.errBadCredentials: Jira refused that email and token. The token may have been revoked, or it may belong to a different account.
jira.errNoSuchSite: There is no Jira site at that address. Check JIRA_BASE_URL in the Supabase dashboard.
jira.errJiraForbidden: That account authenticated, but Jira will not let it read this. Check the account's Jira permissions.
jira.errRateLimited: Jira is rate-limiting this account right now. Wait a moment and try again.
jira.errBadJql: Jira rejected that query — the JQL is not valid on that site.
jira.errTimeout: Jira did not answer in time.
jira.errMissingSecret: The jira-read function is missing at least one of its three secrets. Set JIRA_BASE_URL, JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN in the Supabase dashboard.
jira.errBadBaseUrl: JIRA_BASE_URL is set but is not a usable https address. It should look like https://your-site.atlassian.net, with no path after it.
jira.errBadEmail: JIRA_EMAIL is set but is not a usable email address. It must be the address of the Atlassian account the API token belongs to.
jira.errGone: Jira says that part of its API no longer exists. The function is calling an endpoint Atlassian has retired, and it needs updating.
jira.errUnreachable: Jira could not be reached at all from the server. The address may be wrong, or the site may be down.
